input.summary: The alert is a true positive and part of a larger attack that hit all three payments-prod clusters. Jordan Doe (jdoe@example.com) is on PTO from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-19 and normally works from darwin. Someone used his identity from 198.51.100.23, a malicious bulletproof VPS IP (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING, NL) listed in threat feeds for k8s API brute-force and an open Docker registry, with a linux kubectl client. The same steps ran on EKS (14:02-14:25Z), then GKE (14:38-15:01Z), then AKS (15:11-15:34Z). On each cluster the actor checked their own permissions, listed namespaces and was denied kube-system secrets and job creation. They then read the payments-db-credentials secret. Next they created a privileged pod (debug-tools-7f9c) with host PID and host network and the node's root filesystem mounted, and used nsenter to get a root shell on the node. From the same IP they then used the argocd-application-controller service account token, most likely stolen from the node, to create a ClusterRoleBinding (jdoe-break-glass) giving jdoe cluster-admin. With that access they installed persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet (kube-metrics-agent) and a CronJob (node-cert-rotate), both pulling images from the attacker's registry at 198.51.100.23:5000, plus a NodePort service on port 30080. Finally they listed secrets across the whole cluster (the alerting event).

evidence.description: privileged hostPID/hostNetwork pod debug-tools-7f9c with hostPath / mounted
exec nsenter --target 1 to escape to the node
stolen argocd SA token used from attacker IP to list clusterrolebindings
argocd SA creates CRB jdoe-break-glass -> cluster-admin
DaemonSet kube-metrics-agent in kube-system using image 198.51.100.23:5000
argocd SA lists CRBs from attacker IP
argocd SA lists CRBs from attacker IP

benign_lookalikes: Routine argocd-application-controller list calls from in-cluster IP 10.0.12.173 with the argocd-application-controller/v2.12.3 user agent: normal GitOps reconciliation, unlike the same SA used from 198.51.100.23 via kubectl.
eks:addon-manager updates to the eks:podsecuritypolicy:authenticated and eks:addon-cluster-admin ClusterRoleBindings at 03:05Z from 10.0.0.10: managed EKS add-on maintenance.

Interactive sh/bash execs into application pods by SRE and developer staff (hana.rossi, blake.petrov, wes.tanaka, tara.jensen, rosa.kowalski, vera.fischer, rpatel, gabe.garcia, wes.okafor) from corporate 203.0.113.x IPs: ordinary app debugging, with no nsenter and no privileged pods.
